chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whatever is a matter of obedience to Allah that a man undertakes, it is incumbent upon him to fulfill it. And whatever is a matter of disobedience to Allah that a man undertakes, it is incumbent upon him to abandon it in favor of obedience to Allah."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fulfilling vows made for obedience or disobedience to Allah?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*'s chapter on Vows (*Bab al-Nudhur*), Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the theological mechanics of vow fulfillment, distinguishing between vows of obedience which are binding and vows of sin which must be expiated by abandonment. This narration underscores the Shia juristic principle that the validity of a vow is contingent upon its alignment with divine command, ensuring that human commitments do not become obstacles to worship.
